## Fact Sheet (all numbers from raw JSONs)

**Run shape.** Phase-0 gate fired `GO-descoped`: only 3 of the 23 new candidates beat the old panel max −3.10 (carpenter −3.003, custodian −3.032, stenographer −3.091; GO-full needed 4), so the run trained 3 source arms × 3 seeds (9 cells, not 12): marine_biologist (prior −3.403), courthouse_architecture_historian (−3.229), wooden_furniture_carpenter (−3.003, new top-prior persona). Panel = 24 (15 nested originals + 9 new), strata H/M/L at {−3.25, −3.40}; H stratum now has 10 personas (was 2-3 in the parent). Base-FP screen: all 24 panel personas at 0% base `stated_seven` on headline framings → the trained−base adjusted DV is identical to the raw DV everywhere.

**P1 — prior robustness (within-arm).** Full-panel Spearman ρ(prior, leak), n=23 personas per arm:
- marine: ρ = 0.764 (p = 0.00002); seed-level cluster bootstrap mean 0.447, 95% CI [0.305, 0.568]
- courthouse-historian: ρ = 0.742 (p = 0.00005); bootstrap mean 0.610, 95% CI [0.348, 0.777]
- carpenter: ρ = 0.621 (p = 0.0016); bootstrap mean 0.487, 95% CI [0.299, 0.628]
All three CIs exclude 0. Drop-one (marine): stable 0.74–0.80 across all 23 single-persona removals — the parent's single-persona leverage problem is gone. Drop-top-stratum (remove all 10 H personas): ρ = 0.121 (n=13), 0.367 (n=14), 0.163 (n=14); critical ρ at those n ≈ 0.53–0.55; per the pre-registered reading discipline, courthouse-historian reads "positive but underpowered", marine and carpenter read "weak positive" (below the 0.2 band). Within-stratum leak medians (marine): L 0.119, M 0.119, H 0.225 — flat below the H boundary. All 3 arms pass the ≥30%-above-1% informativeness rule (23/23, 10/23, 8/23).

**Verdict P1: partially supported.** Not falsified (no arm has CI including 0 or drop-stratum ρ ≤ 0); not confirmed at the pre-registered bar (no arm reaches drop-stratum ρ ≥ 0.2 with p < 0.10 — the closest is courthouse-historian at 0.367, p = 0.20). The honest read: the prior→leak relationship replicates at panel level and survives de-leveraging, but it is carried by the high-prior stratum as a block; within the low/mid strata the prior does not rank personas. Restriction-of-range caveat applies to the drop-stratum read (dropping H removes ~60% of the prior axis).

**P2 — source prior → gating tightness.** Median leak over the 21 shared bystanders: 13.7% (marine, prior −3.40) → 0.37% (courthouse-historian, −3.23) → 0.12% (carpenter, −3.00). Perfect monotone decreasing; zero hard inversions (seed-range overlap rule). Per plan §7 the descoped 3-arm branch is directional only — no permutation p claimed. Pooled per-(arm × seed) Spearman −0.834 (9 points) is descriptive only. Texture that cuts against a weak-implant alternative: the panel-MAX leak rises 38.5% → 47.2% → 90.6% across the same ordering (furniture_historian adopts the fact on 245/270 headline rows under the carpenter teacher), so high-prior teachers install a strong, narrowly-propagating implant rather than a weak one. **Verdict P2: supported, directional (n=3 arms).** Carried caveats: source-provenance confound (the top arm's teacher is a new, designed-for-this-experiment persona); no source self-rate exists (source excluded from its own eval panel, inherited design).

**P3 — content-fit vs string-prior (pre-treatment conditioning).** Collinearity gate NOT tripped: Pearson(prior, base_on_topic) = 0.208 (expected to trip at 0.6 — it didn't, because base on-topic barely varies). Partial ρ(prior, leak | base_length, base_on_topic): marine 0.766 (vs 0.764 unadjusted; persona-level bootstrap 95% CI [0.532, 0.885]), courthouse-historian 0.708 (vs 0.742; CI [0.439, 0.861]), carpenter 0.557 (vs 0.621; CI [0.231, 0.777]) — 90–100% retention, all CIs exclude 0. Outcome-B partials ρ(base_on_topic, leak | prior) span 0 in all arms (−0.21, +0.24, +0.18). **BUT the pre-registered covariate-reliability gate fails:** between-persona SD of base_on_topic = 0.075 < 2× median subsample SE (2 × 0.052 = 0.105); range 0.55–0.92. Per plan §4.4 the pre-registered verdict is **covariate-underpowered, not Outcome A**: base topic-engagement is nearly uniform across personas on these fact-eliciting probes, so the run had little power to detect engagement-proxying. Directionally consistent with Outcome A (prior is real beyond engagement), not claimable as such.

## Interpretation

The de-leveraging worked, and it sharpened rather than killed the parent's claim. The parent's headline rested on 2 high-prior personas; with 10 of them, the full-panel correlation replicates in every arm (0.62–0.76) and no single persona matters (drop-one flat). What the enrichment reveals is the SHAPE of the relationship: it's a threshold/stratum effect, not a graded ranking — personas above the −3.25 prior boundary leak ~2× the rest (marine arm), and below that boundary the prior carries no rank information. For the predictor program, that means "compute the bystander prior and threshold it" is supported; "use the prior as a continuous risk score" is not.

The new monotone gating result is the more decision-relevant finding: the teacher's own measured prior on the fact predicts how tightly the implant stays locked to the teacher (panel-median leak collapses two orders of magnitude across a 0.4-nat source-prior range), while the implant itself stays strong (nearest-neighbor adoption rises to 91%). Alternative explanations that survive: (a) weaker effective training signal under high-prior teachers (no source self-rate to rule it out — though the 91% neighbor adoption argues the implant is not weak); (b) provenance confound (designed-new vs pre-existing personas co-vary with prior; n=3 arms cannot deconfound).

P3 is the run's main miss, and it failed in an informative way: the engagement covariate cannot proxy-test the prior because base topic-engagement is essentially uniform when probes are fact-eliciting (everyone discusses the courthouse when asked about the courthouse). A future engagement covariate needs probes where engagement can vary (e.g., open-ended chat, not entity-named elicitation).

**Confidence: MODERATE** — binding constraints: single invented fact + single recipe (generalization unknown); the gating monotonicity is a 3-point directional ordering; the stratum-contrast read is partly a restriction-of-range artifact of the drop-stratum test design.

**Headline claim:** Bystander prior still predicts fact leakage on a panel enriched with high-prior personas, but as a high-vs-rest stratum contrast rather than a graded ranking; higher-prior teachers gate panel-wide leakage monotonically tighter while leaking hardest to their nearest high-prior neighbor.

## Codex Interpretation Critique — Round 1

**Verdict: REVISE**

### Overclaims
- "the teacher-side prior looks like a control knob for gating tightness" — the Goal allows testing source-prior association, but the evidence is only a 3-arm descoped ordering with a new-persona provenance confound — weaken to "directional evidence that source prior may track tighter gating."
- "high-prior teachers don't train weaker implants; the fact just propagates to fewer, closer personas" — no teacher self-rate exists, and one high nearest-neighbor rate does not rule out weaker global training — weaken to "not obviously a failed implant; nearest-neighbor adoption argues against a pure weak-implant explanation."
- "the prior is a real, teacher-independent predictor" — source-proximity/topical-neighbor effects are positive in the high-prior arms, so "teacher-independent" is too strong — weaken to "replicated across the three tested teachers, with source-proximity still needing separation."
- "not explained away by pre-training topic engagement" — the covariate reliability gate failed, so this covariate could not explain it away; topic engagement in general was not ruled out — revise to "not explained away by this saturated entity-named engagement covariate."

### Surprising Unmentioned Patterns
- Source proximity is not null in this run — `predictors.json` shows `partial_spearman_cos_to_source_given_prior` = 0.536 for the carpenter arm with positive bootstrap CI, and courthouse-historian has positive source-cosine signal too — this matters because the "teacher prior gates tighter" result may partly be source-neighbor topology.
- The carpenter arm has large non-H / boundary-adjacent surface-affinity leakage — `antiques_dealer` leaks 24.9% despite prior −3.258, below the H cutoff — this weakens a pure high-vs-rest threshold story and points to furniture-surface affinity.
- Several high-leak cells have large seed heterogeneity — e.g. carpenter→courthouse_architecture_historian is 0.0 / 40.4% / 10.4%, and carpenter→antiques_dealer is 0.7% / 33.3% / 40.7% in `predictors.json` — the prose should mention that some "narrow gating" structure is seed-sensitive.

### Alternative Explanations Not Addressed
- The source-prior gating finding could be explained by source-topical proximity rather than source prior — rule it out with arms that vary prior while holding source-neighbor structure/provenance fixed, or report the existing cosine/proximity stats as an unresolved confound.
- The "not weaker implant" claim could be explained by one local neighbor receiving the implant while the teacher itself or broader source neighborhood remains unknown — add a teacher self-assertion eval or weaken the claim.
- The engagement-control null could be explained by a saturated covariate from entity-named prompts — the body partly says this, but the headline/figure language should not imply topic engagement was broadly ruled out.

## Interpretation

The de-leveraging worked and sharpened the parent's claim: with 10 high-prior personas, the full-panel correlation replicates in every arm (0.62–0.76) and no single persona matters. The SHAPE is a threshold/stratum effect, not a graded ranking — personas above −3.25 leak ~2× the rest (marine arm), below it the prior carries no rank information. For the predictor program: "compute the bystander prior and threshold it" is supported; "use it as a continuous risk score" is not.

The teacher-side result is directional evidence that the teacher's measured prior tracks gating tightness: panel-median leak collapses from 13.7% under the low-prior teacher to under half a percent under both high-prior teachers (the bottom two arms are indistinguishable at floor), while the implant stays strong where it does land (nearest-neighbor adoption up to 90.6%). P3 failed informatively: base topic-engagement is nearly uniform on entity-named probes (everyone discusses the courthouse when asked about it), so this covariate could not have explained the prior away even if engagement were the true driver. A real test needs probes where engagement can vary.

**Headline claim:** Bystander prior still predicts fact leakage on a panel enriched with high-prior personas, but as a high-vs-rest stratum contrast rather than a graded ranking; the teacher-side prior shows directional evidence of tighter panel-wide gating, with the leak concentrating on the teacher's nearest-neighbor persona.

### 1. Teacher self-assertion eval on the existing 9 adapters — Diagnostic

**Parent:** #541
**question_relation:** same
**followup_label:** teacher-self-assertion-eval
**Goal:** Test whether the bystander-prior→leakage relationship found in #500 holds on a persona panel deliberately enriched with high-prior personas (de-leveraging the two outliers that carried the #500 headline), and whether the source persona's MEASURED prior on the fact predicts panel-wide gating tightness, by re-running the #500 design with a prior-stratified bystander panel and source personas selected by measured base prior instead of hand-coded content-relatedness.
**Hypothesis:** The two high-prior teachers self-assert the taught fact at high rates under their own persona (comparable to or above the marine arm's panel-wide leak), so the panel-wide lockdown is narrow propagation, not a weak implant.
**Falsification:** If the courthouse-historian and carpenter teachers self-assert at floor (within seed-range of their own panel medians, <1%), the gating finding collapses to "high-prior teachers train weaker implants" and the narrower-not-weaker read in the TL;DR is killed.
**Differs from parent:** Exactly one change — each arm's eval panel adds the arm's own teacher persona (the parent design excluded each teacher from its own panel, so no self-rate exists).

**Pre-filled spec (from parent):**
- Model: same (the 9 trained LoRA cells; no new training)
- Data: same 270 headline eval rows (12 framings), generated under the teacher's own system prompt
- Seeds: same (42/137/256)
- Eval: same on-policy temp-0 vLLM recipe, same 5-way Haiku judge
- Config: same EXCEPT eval panel = teacher persona only (per cell), reported as teacher self-assertion rate per arm per seed

**Artifact-premise verification (this proposal):** `huggingface_hub.list_repo_files('superkaiba1/explore-persona-space-overflow', revision='9184fcca...')` run for this proposal lists all 9 cells `adapters/exp541-{arm}-on_policy_suppression_cn-seed{42,137,256}/` at 11 files each (99 total) with `adapter_model.safetensors` present in every cell. Nothing missing.

**Estimated cost:** ~2 GPU-hours on 1× H100 (eval intent; 9 adapter loads × 270 generations + Batch judging)
**If it works:** Rules the weak-implant alternative in or out for the gating finding — directly strengthens or rewrites a load-bearing TL;DR claim.
**If it fails (teachers at floor):** Equally informative — the gating result is reinterpreted as implant-strength variation, and the second-fact replication (proposal 3) becomes about implant strength vs teacher prior instead.

**auto_run:** yes
**auto_run_reason:** Single corrective measurement gap-fill with a fully grounded recipe, verified artifacts (Hub listing above), known ~2 GPU-h cost, no design/taste decision.

**cost_class:** needs-gpu
**headline_affecting:** yes

### 2. Engagement covariate re-test on open-ended, non-entity-named probes — Diagnostic

**Parent:** #541
**question_relation:** same
**followup_label:** open-ended-engagement-covariate
**Goal:** Test whether the bystander-prior→leakage relationship found in #500 holds on a persona panel deliberately enriched with high-prior personas (de-leveraging the two outliers that carried the #500 headline), and whether the source persona's MEASURED prior on the fact predicts panel-wide gating tightness, by re-running the #500 design with a prior-stratified bystander panel and source personas selected by measured base prior instead of hand-coded content-relatedness.
**Hypothesis:** With probes that do not name the courthouse (topic-adjacent open-ended prompts: small-town landmarks, interesting buildings, "what are you into"), base topic-engagement varies between personas, and partialling it out leaves the prior–leak correlation intact.
**Falsification:** If the engagement-given-prior partial is significant and the prior-given-engagement partial spans zero, the H1 claim is confounded — the prior was a proxy for topic engagement all along.
**Differs from parent:** Exactly one change — the probe set on which the pre-treatment engagement covariate is measured (open-ended, entity not named) replacing the saturated entity-named version; leak outcomes, personas, judge, and partial-correlation analysis all reuse the committed #541 data (`eval_results/issue_541/predictors.json` + `base_engagement_covariates.json`, verified present on main).

**Pre-filled spec (from parent):**
- Model: same frozen base (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct), no training
- Data: ~60 new open-ended probes × 24 personas (base completions only)
- Seeds: n/a (deterministic temp-0 generation, single pass as in parent covariate)
- Eval: same Haiku binary on-topic judge + same cluster-bootstrap partial-correlation code (`scripts/issue541_engagement.py`, `scripts/issue541_predictors.py`)
- Config: same EXCEPT covariate probe set

**Estimated cost:** ~1 GPU-hour on 1× H100 (1,440 base generations; judging via Batch API)
**If it works:** Resolves the covariate-underpowered verdict — the most decision-relevant rival to the headline gets a real test.
**If it fails (floor saturation — nobody spontaneously mentions courthouses):** We learn the engagement construct needs a graded topic-affinity probe ladder, bounding future covariate designs; zero training wasted.

**auto_run:** no
**auto_run_reason:** The open-ended probe set + topic rubric is a construct-definition choice with symmetric failure modes (ceiling saturation in the parent vs floor saturation here) — needs a human check before running.

**cost_class:** needs-gpu
**headline_affecting:** yes

### 3. Second-fact replication with pre-existing, proximity-decoupled teachers — Reproduction

**Parent:** #541
**question_relation:** substantially-different
**Goal:** Test whether the high-prior-stratum bystander-leakage contrast and the teacher-prior-to-gating relationship generalize to a second invented fact, using pre-existing (not purpose-written) teacher personas selected so that measured base prior and persona-activation proximity to the panel are decoupled.
**Hypothesis:** Both effects replicate on a new fact: the high-prior stratum leaks ~2x the rest, and higher-prior teachers gate tighter even when their activation-cosine to the panel is low — separating prior from teacher-neighborhood topology.
**Falsification:** If the high-prior stratum does not leak more on the new fact, the #541 headline is fact-specific; if low-proximity high-prior teachers do NOT gate tightly, the gating effect was teacher-neighborhood topology, not prior.
**Differs from parent:** Exactly one change at the replication level — the taught fact (and the consequent prescreen-selected panel/teachers, with the teacher-selection rule additionally constrained to decouple prior from proximity, breaking the provenance and topology confounds simultaneously).

**Pre-filled spec (from parent):**
- Model: same (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, LoRA r=32 α=64, lr 2e-4, 1 epoch, contrastive 100/200/600 mix)
- Data: new invented fact via the #444 fact-pick protocol; fresh Phase-0 prior prescreen
- Seeds: same (3 per arm)
- Eval: same on-policy 5-way-judge recipe, 270 rows/persona/seed, teacher INCLUDED in own panel (folding in proposal 1's fix)
- Config: same EXCEPT the fact + teacher-selection rule (measured prior decoupled from panel cosine; no purpose-written personas)

**Estimated cost:** ~25 GPU-hours on 4× H100 (parent science cost ~20 GPU-h; infra fixes now landed; + prescreen)
**If it works:** Elevates both findings from single-fact MODERATE to a generalizing claim, with the prior-vs-topology mechanism separated.
**If it fails:** The predictor program learns the prior signal is fact- or provenance-bound — redirects toward topic-engagement / topology predictors.

**auto_run:** no
**auto_run_reason:** Needs its own adversarial plan — fact pick, panel rebuild, and the decoupled teacher-selection criterion are design decisions, not a single grounded diff.

**cost_class:** needs-gpu
**headline_affecting:** no
